interface.signature: def solve(T: int, test_cases: list[tuple[int, int, int, int, int, list[tuple[int, int, int]]]]) -> list[str]: ...

preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is between 1 and 3 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= K <= N <= 10**5 for N, K, _, _, _ in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of cities N is between 2 and 10^5, and the number of old cities K is between 2 and N.

preconditions.expression: all(0 <= M <= 10**5 for _, _, _, M, _ in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of newer roads M is between 0 and 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= S <= N for _, _, _, _, S in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the starting city S is between 1 and N.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= N and 1 <= b_i <= N and a_i != b_i for _, _, _, _, _, roads in test_cases for a_i, b_i, _ in roads)
preconditions.description: For each test case, every newer road connects two distinct cities a_i and b_i, each between 1 and N.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= c_i <= 10**9 for _, _, _, _, _, roads in test_cases for _, _, c_i in roads)
preconditions.description: For each test case, every newer road length c_i is between 1 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set((a_i, b_i) for a_i, b_i, _ in roads)) == len(roads) for _, _, _, _, _, roads in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, all newer roads are distinct (no duplicate pairs).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= X <= 10**9 for _, X, _, _, _ in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the length X of roads between old cities is between 1 and 10^9.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one line per test case.

postconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == N for line in output)
postconditions.description: Each output line contains exactly N integers, one for each city.

postconditions.expression: all(all(0 <= int(dist) <= 10**18 for dist in line.split()) for line in output)
postconditions.description: Each distance in the output is a non-negative integer (up to 10^18).

postconditions.expression: all(int(line.split()[S_idx - 1]) == 0 for (_, _, _, _, S_idx, _), line in zip(test_cases, output))
postconditions.description: The distance from city S to itself is always 0.

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(line.split()[i - 1]) == int(line.split()[j - 1]) or int(line.split()[i - 1]) < int(line.split()[j - 1]) for i in range(1, N + 1) for j in range(1, N + 1) if i != j) for (N, _, _, _, _, _), line in zip(test_cases, output))
postconditions.description: The computed distances are consistent with the shortest-path property (transitivity).

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(line.split()[i - 1]) == min(int(line.split()[i - 1]), int(line.split()[j - 1]) + c) for (N, K, X, _, S_idx, roads), line in zip(test_cases, output) for a_i, b_i, c in roads for i in range(1, N + 1) if (a_i == i and b_i == S_idx) or (b_i == i and a_i == S_idx)) for i in range(1, N + 1))
postconditions.description: The computed distances respect the newer roads' lengths (direct connections).

postconditions.expression: all(all(int(line.split()[i - 1]) == X for (N, K, X, _, S_idx, _), line in zip(test_cases, output) for i in range(1, K + 1) if i != S_idx) for (N, K, _, _, S_idx, _) in test_cases)
postconditions.description: The distance between any two old cities (1..K) is exactly X, if no shorter path exists via newer roads.
